subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: How a Coal Power Plant Works
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How a Coal Power Plant Works.

hook.text: A coal plant burns rock to boil water to spin a magnet to push electrons. Four steps to make electricity.

buildup.text: Pulverized coal burns at 1,400 degrees C. The heat boils water into high-pressure steam that drives a turbine.

discovery.text: The turbine spins a generator at 3,000 rpm. Electromagnetic induction converts mechanical energy into electrical current.

twist.text: Even the best coal plants waste 60% of fuel energy as heat. Cooling towers dump it into the atmosphere.

climax.text: Coal still generates 36% of global electricity. It's cheap but produces more CO2 per kilowatt than any other source.

punchline.text: Burn rock. Boil water. Spin magnets. That's most of the grid.

quiz.question: Why do coal power plants waste 60% of fuel energy?
options: Coal burns incompletely, leaving unburned carbon in the ash
Thermodynamic limits and cooling losses dump most heat into the atmosphere
Friction in the generator converts most energy into unwanted vibration
